name: WFW World Heavyweight Title
notes: The fed's broadcast says this title and the North American Title "resume and carry on the lineage of the old NGEN World Heavyweight Title" (Vox Hiberionacum, March 2003), and a commentator calls it "descended from both the NGEN & BAD World Heavyweight Titles" (Rage in the Cage). These are the fed's claims; its first champion was crowned in 2003 and no earlier reign is carried onto this title. The fed's own post of its champions, headed "NGEN/WFW World Heavyweight Title History" (December 2003, kept up in later years), begins with Doc Silver at Vox Hiberionacum and carries no NGEN reign; it dates each change a few days after the first post of the broadcast that told it. The same list dates the Michaels, Edmunds and Wylde changes to 31 December 2003, 25 February 2004 and 21 March 2004, a few days after the first posts of the broadcasts that told them (30 December 2003, 18 February 2004 and 10 March 2004), which this wing's rows use. The same list dates the Manson change to 29 April 2004, the day the post telling the ladder match went up; this wing's rows use the date of the first post of the broadcast, 18 April 2004.
epitaph: Created for a fourteen-man tournament that began at the Curt Hennig Memorial Show and ended with a three-way at Vox Hiberionacum on 29 March 2003, where Doc Silver became the first champion. Psycho took it from him in a four-way at the first pay-per-view and Silver escaped a razor-wire cage to win it back three weeks later. Shawn Hart took it from him two falls to one at the Spirit of NGEN on 16 August 2003, winning the last fall, a Last Man Standing match, on the special referee's ten count. Hart kept it against Luster at New World Madness in October 2003 and against Michael Manson in a Chicago street fight at Ghoulish Games, the fed's pay-per-view of 15 November. Scotty Michaels took it from Hart in a Winter Wonderland match in Central Park at Merrython on 30 December 2003, with Luster's help; Sean Edmunds won it from him in a sixty-minute Ironman match at Great Expectations on 18 February 2004, five falls to four; and Alex Wylde, the fed's President, won it from Edmunds at Road to Glory on 10 March 2004. Michael Manson took it from Wylde in a ladder match at the Superbowl of Wrestling on 18 April 2004, with Joey Melton as special referee, and kept it against Richard Gideon at BOMB Voyage on 9 June 2004. Manson kept it against Felix Red at Cherry Blossom Chaos II on 15 August 2004. Manson kept it against El Arco Iris, two falls to one under Lucha rules, at Guerra Interminable on 3 November 2004.

name: WFW North American Title
notes: Introduced beside the World Heavyweight Title as the fed's second belt; the Vox Hiberionacum introduction says both resume the lineage of the old NGEN World Heavyweight Title, a claim of the fed's own. While Rat Fink held the stolen belt, the broadcasts went on calling Michael Manson champion. The fed's own post of its North American champions, headed "NGEN/WFW North American Title History" (December 2003, kept up in later years), begins with Michael Manson at Vox Hiberionacum and carries no NGEN reign; like the World title's list, it dates each change a few days after the first post of the broadcast that told it. The same list dates the Psycho change to 26 April 2004, the day the post telling the deciding fall went up; this wing's rows use the date of the first post of the broadcast, 18 April 2004.
epitaph: Won by Michael Manson on 29 March 2003 as the man left unpinned in the three-way final for the World Heavyweight Title. Rat Fink stole the belt in April, and Manson won it back in a ladder match at the first pay-per-view in May. Scotty Michaels took it from Manson in a steel cage at the Spirit of NGEN on 16 August 2003, after Luster struck Manson with a pipe, and kept it against Copycat at Almost Live. Richard Gideon took it from Scotty Michaels in a three-way with Felix Red at Ghoulish Games on 15 November 2003, when Michaels passed out in his figure-four leglock, and kept it against Psycho at Turkey Day Terror on 8 December when Psycho was disqualified for using a fork. Gideon kept it in a three-way against Copycat and Psycho at Great Expectations on 18 February 2004. Psycho took it from Gideon at the Superbowl of Wrestling on 18 April 2004, two falls to one in a match of submissions only, the Four Corners of Hell and a Texas Death Match. Psycho kept it against Rat Fink, Pulsar and El Arco Iris at Cherry Blossom Chaos II on 15 August 2004 and against Golem at Paradise Lost on 20 September 2004.

name: BAD World Heavyweight Title
notes: The fed presents this as the title of the old BAD promotion and, until 16 August 2003, held it together with the WFW World Heavyweight Title; that night Shawn Hart, who had just won both, handed it to Diablo to be defended "hardcore style" under falls-count-anywhere, no-disqualification, no-countout rules. No earlier BAD reign is carried onto this title. The fed's own post, headed B.A.D. World Heavyweight Title History (first posted 6 January 2005 and kept up to 2010), repeats the reigns of the unified title before the 16 August 2003 split and dates the later changes a few days after this wing's show rows (Shawn Hart's win over Doc Silver on 20 August 2003, Rat Fink's on 7 September, Felix Red's on 10 December, Minion's on 23 February 2004, Jared Wells's on 22 April) and Minion's vacating on 10 March 2004 at Road to Glory, where this wing's row dates it from the line-up of 27 March; this wing's rows use the dates of the broadcasts and, for the 2007 and 2009 changes, which only the list tells, the list's own dates.
epitaph: Separated from the WFW World Heavyweight Title on 16 August 2003, when Shawn Hart handed it to Diablo. Rat Fink took it from Diablo in Central Park, helped by The American and Fink Bot, and kept it against Psycho in a no-disqualification brawl at Almost Live. Rat Fink kept it against Pulsar at Ghoulish Games, but Felix Red took it from him at Turkey Day Terror on 8 December 2003 with the help of two fans, and won a tag match beside Richard Gideon at Merrython. Felix Red kept it against Psycho at Mind Over Matter on 22 January 2004, and Minion took it from him in a falls-count-anywhere match at Great Expectations on 18 February 2004; the line-up announced at Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux on 27 March says Minion vacated it with a torn ligament. Jared Wells won the vacant title in a four-man falls count anywhere elimination match at the Superbowl of Wrestling on 18 April 2004 and kept it against Mike Lane at BOMB Voyage on 9 June 2004. Jared Wells kept it against Iron Lion at Cherry Blossom Chaos II on 15 August 2004. The fed's own history of the belt has Steve Johnson take it from Wells on 17 April 2007, ending a reign of almost three years, and Wells beat Johnson at Unplugged on 31 December 2009; the fed carried the title into its NGEN relaunch with Wells as champion on 20 January 2010.
